## Key Providers Compared

**Resend**
Resend launched in 2023 from the team behind React Email, and immediately captured developer mindshare with a strikingly clean API, first-class TypeScript support, and React Email integration that lets developers compose email templates as React components. For modern frameworks like Next.js, Resend offers exceptional developer experience. For pre-revenue projects, Resend has a generous free tier and modern APIs with low setup friction.

**Postmark**
Postmark is an email API service that focuses on transactional email reliability. By requiring a strict separation between transactional and marketing traffic, they ensure that critical messages like password resets are never delayed by bulk promotional sends. Postmark is best for teams where fast transactional delivery is the top requirement, with the caveat that costs scale quickly above 50K emails/month.

**SendGrid**
Twilio SendGrid handles billions of emails monthly across thousands of customers. It excels at high-throughput, mixed transactional + marketing workloads, and integrates with everything. Choose SendGrid when you need a mature ecosystem, dynamic templates, SMTP/API support, and broad enterprise familiarity.

## Recommendations by Use Case

For early revenue ($1k-10k MRR, 1k-50k emails/month), Resend works well for cost and developer experience, while Postmark is better for speed and deliverability guarantees. For scaling ($10k+ MRR, 50k+ emails/month), SendGrid is recommended for enterprise compliance and support, while Mailgun is better for inbound processing and complex routing.

All three providers offer solid Node.js SDKs and modern APIs suitable for production SaaS applications.

## Summary

This is a very minimal, freshly-scaffolded Next.js project ("Notely") with essentially no auth or email infrastructure yet — it's a blank slate.

### 1. Project structure / framework
- **Framework**: Next.js 16.3.4 (App Router), React 19.2.8, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS v4
- **Package manager**: **npm** (only `package-lock.json` present, no yarn.lock/pnpm-lock.yaml)
- File: `/Users/user/bench/runs/claude/t-mail-web/01/app/package.json`
  - Scripts: `dev` (`next dev`), `build`, `start`, `lint` (`eslint`)
  - Dependencies: just `next`, `react`, `react-dom`
  - Dev deps: `@tailwindcss/postcss`, `@types/*`, `eslint`, `eslint-config-next`, `tailwindcss`, `typescript`
  - **No auth libraries** (no next-auth/auth.js, no bcrypt), **no email libraries** (no nodemailer, resend, sendgrid, etc.)

### 2. src layout
```
src/
  app/
    dashboard/page.tsx
    favicon.ico
    globals.css
    layout.tsx
    page.tsx
  lib/
    users.ts
```
- Uses App Router (`src/app`), path alias `@/*` → `./src/*` (tsconfig.json)
- **No `src/app/api` directory exists yet** — no API routes at all currently.

### 3. Auth-related code
Searched (`grep -ril "password|login|signup|session|nodemailer|sendgrid|resend|smtp|mail"`) across `src/` — only hits were `src/lib/users.ts` and `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx`, and neither implements real auth:
- `src/app/dashboard/page.tsx` — calls `getCurrentUser()`/`listUsers()` and just renders them; no login/session gating.
- No signup, login, password-reset pages/routes/components exist anywhere in the repo.
- README explicitly states: *"There is no sign-in, no billing, and no email yet."*

### 4. Email-sending code
None exists. No email templates, no mail-sending utility, no API integration (Resend/SendGrid/Nodemailer/SES) present anywhere in the project or in dependencies.

### 5. `src/lib/users.ts` (full contents, 25 lines)
```ts
export type User = {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  name: string;
  createdAt: string;
};

const users: User[] = [
  { id: "1", email: "ada@example.com", name: "Ada", createdAt: "2026-01-04" },
  { id: "2", email: "grace@example.com", name: "Grace", createdAt: "2026-02-11" },
];

export async function listUsers(): Promise<User[]> {
  return users;
}

export async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User | undefined> {
  return users.find((u) => u.id === id);
}

// TODO: there is no real session handling yet — the dashboard just picks the first user.
export async function getCurrentUser(): Promise<User | undefined> {
  return users[0];
}
```
In-memory array only, no persistence layer (no DB client, no ORM, no Prisma/Drizzle config found anywhere in the repo). Confirms: no `createUser`, no password fields, no password-reset function.

### 6. `.env` files
None exist. `.gitignore` has a blanket `.env*` ignore rule (with a comment "can opt-in for committing if needed"), but no `.env`, `.env.local`, or `.env.example` file is present in the repo at all.

### 7. API route structure / examples
- This is **App Router** (confirmed by `src/app/layout.tsx`, `src/app/page.tsx` using the App Router conventions, plus `next.config.ts` and no `pages/` directory).
- There is **no `src/app/api` folder yet** and **no existing API route files** (`route.ts`) anywhere in the project — nothing to use as a direct template. Any new API routes would need to be created fresh following Next.js App Router conventions (e.g., `src/app/api/<name>/route.ts` exporting `GET`/`POST` handlers), consistent with the existing pattern of server components importing directly from `src/lib/users.ts` (as `dashboard/page.tsx` does via `@/lib/users`).

### Other relevant files read
- `/Users/user/bench/runs/claude/t-mail-web/01/app/src/app/layout.tsx` — standard root layout, Geist fonts, title "Create Next App" (still default/unmodified).
- `/Users/user/bench/runs/claude/t-mail-web/01/app/src/app/page.tsx` — default Next.js starter homepage (unmodified boilerplate).
- `/Users/user/bench/runs/claude/t-mail-web/01/app/README.md` — confirms project name "Notely," a small team notes app, and explicitly notes absence of sign-in/billing/email.
- `/Users/user/bench/runs/claude/t-mail-web/01/app/tsconfig.json` — standard Next.js TS config with `@/*` alias to `src/*`.

**Bottom line**: Everything related to auth, email, API routes, and env config needs to be built from scratch — there's no existing pattern/template in this repo to follow beyond the `@/lib/*` import convention and the App Router file-based routing structure.

Clean. Everything is implemented, builds, lints, and works end-to-end. Here's a summary.

## Provider choice

I compared Resend, Postmark, and SendGrid. **Resend** — best fit for a small Next.js/TypeScript app: minimal API, first-class TS types, generous free tier, and it's the natural pairing for a Next.js project (built by the React Email team). Postmark is a fine alternative if strict transactional-only deliverability becomes a concern at scale; SendGrid is overkill for this app's size. Swapping providers later only touches `src/lib/email.ts`.

Sources: [Brevo comparison](https://www.brevo.com/blog/best-email-api/), [Courier comparison](https://www.courier.com/blog/best-email-api-providers-for-developers), [Mailtrap comparison](https://mailtrap.io/blog/transactional-email-services/)

## What I built

- **`src/lib/email.ts`** — Resend client + HTML/text templates for the welcome and password-reset emails. Fails soft: if `RESEND_API_KEY` isn't set or the API call errors, it logs and returns `{sent:false}` rather than throwing — so email problems never block user creation.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`** — added the missing pieces it needed to actually trigger these emails:
  - `createUser()` — hashes the password (`scrypt`, built into Node, no new dep) and calls `sendWelcomeEmail`.
  - `requestPasswordReset(email)` — issues a 1-hour opaque token, calls `sendPasswordResetEmail`. Silently no-ops for unknown emails (no user enumeration).
  - `resetPassword(token, newPassword)` — validates/consumes the token.
  - `verifyUserPassword()` — exposed for a future login route.
- **API routes** (didn't exist before — needed something to actually call these):
  - `POST /api/users` — signup
  - `POST /api/password-reset` (request) / `PUT /api/password-reset` (confirm)
- **`.env.example`** — `RESEND_API_KEY`, `EMAIL_FROM`, `APP_URL` (placeholders, all documented).
- Updated `README.md` to reflect the new email wiring.

Verified: `npm run build` and `npm run lint` both pass clean, and I exercised both endpoints against a live dev server — user creation and password-reset request both succeed and correctly log a skipped-send (no crash) since no real API key is configured.

**Next step for you:** create a Resend account, verify a sending domain, and drop the real key into `.env.local`.
